previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted following a fall at home after an episode of severe nausea and vomiting, in the setting of alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis. He reported persistent nausea worsening since his last hospitalization, when spironolactone was increased to 300 mg daily. Workup revealed no acute intracranial injury on repeat head CT, and telemetry showed no arrhythmias. A single positive blood culture for gram-positive cocci was deemed a contaminant, and vancomycin was discontinued. Nausea was attributed to portal gastropathy and gastroparesis related to cirrhosis, with possible contribution from medication side effects. He did not vomit during hospitalization, tolerated oral liquids, and was discharged on oral ondansetron for breakthrough nausea. His liver disease remained stable with a MELD score of 11, no ascites on ultrasound, and no evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence. He is currently at the top of the transplant list for his blood type and was advised on nutritional support and close follow-up with hepatology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with HCV and EtOH cirrhosis on transplant list and ___ s/p 
RFA and TACE admitted with nausea, vomiting, and dizziness, with 
multiple previous admissions for similar constellation of 
symptoms over the past several months without clear etiology.

# Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain. No sign of infection with no 
fever, leukocytosis, or other localizing sign. Unclear etiology. 
We stopped patient's iron supplement and his nausea improved, so 
this could have contributed, especially given moderate fecal 
load seen on CT scan. Patient also has a history of chronic 
inactive duodenitis seen on duodenal biopsy in ___, and on 
endoscopy during this admission, the polyp was again seen with 
significant friability.  Biopsy was not repeated given risk of 
bled. A gastric emptying study showed moderately delayed gastric 
emptying. Patient was treated symptomatically, and improved over 
the course of his hospitalization. Patient's diet was advanced 
and he tolerated solid and liquid foods at time of discharge. H. 
Pylori serum test was pending at time of discharge. 

# Metabolic alkalosis. Patient presented with a low anion gap of 
3 on admission. This was likely contraction alkalosis due to 
vomiting. He improved with supportive care. Day of discharge 
HCO3 was 30 and AG was 6. We held his diuretics initially as he 
appeared hypovolemic. On day of discharge, patient was euvolemic 
on exam, tolerating PO, and we restarted his furosemide at 60mg 
and reduced his spironolactone from 300mg to 200mg daily.

# HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis. Listed for transplant. Patient 
has history of hepatic encephalopathy, variceal bleeding, and 
SBP. He will require continued lactulose and rifaximin titrating 
to ___ bowel movements per day. He was also continued on nadolol 
for prior varices (none on recent EGD) and ciprofloxacin for SBP 
prophylaxis.
 
# Ulcerative colitis.  No diarrhea or evidence of colitis on CT 
scan. Continued home mesalamine.  
 

### TRANSITIONAL ISSUES ###
1) We stopped his ferrous sulfate. It may have contributed to 
constipation and abdominal pain.
2) We restarted his furosemide at home 60mg and decreased his 
spironolactone from 300mg daily to 200mg daily.
3) H.pylori serum antigen pending on discharge
4) Duodenal polyp with friability on endoscopy may need repeat 
biopsy in the future

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Cirrhosis secondary to hepatitis C/alcohol, HCC, HE, hypertension,
status post cholecystectomy presenting with nausea, vomiting and dizziness. 
Evaluate for source of pain.

COMPARISON:  Prior abdominal CT from ___ and abdominal MR from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MDCT images were obtained through the abdomen and pelvis
after the uneventful administration of 150 cc Omnipaque intravenous contrast. 
Oral contrast was not provided. Sagittal and coronal reformats were generated.


FINDINGS:

Lung bases are clear.  There is no pleural or pericardial effusion.  

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:  The liver demonstrates a nodular contour, consistent with
known diagnosis of cirrhosis. Post treatment changes are seen in the liver
from known RFA and hyperdensities in the right hepatic lobe are compatible
with prior TACE treatment. Evaluation of residual disease cannot be performed
on this single phase examination.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy
and surgical clips are seen within the right upper quadrant.  The portal vein
is patent. The pancreas and adrenal glands are within normal limits.  There is
mild splenic enlargement measuring 13.5 cm. The kidneys enhance symmetrically
and excrete contrast without evidence of hydronephrosis or masses. 

The stomach is collapsed.  There is no bowel obstruction.  There is no bowel
wall abnormality. The appendix is visualized and there is no evidence of acute
appendicitis. There is moderate fecal loading of the large bowel.  Calcified
structure in the mid small bowel mesentery is again seen and is stable, felt
to represent a retained gallstone.  There is a small fat containing umbilical
hernia.  Note is made of a recanalized umbilical vein, gastroesophageal and
splenic varices and splenorenal shunt. Small cystic lesion in the left
paraortic region is again seen measuring 13 x 12 mm and could represent a
small lymphangioma (2:31). The aorta is of normal diameter and demonstrates
mild atherosclerotic calcifications.  The celiac axis, SMA, bilateral renal
arteries, and ___ are patent. There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph
node enlargement by CT size criteria. There is no free fluid or free air.

CT OF THE PELVIS:  The bladder and terminal ureters are within normal limits. 
The rectum is unremarkable.  There is no pelvic free fluid.  There is no
inguinal or pelvic lymph node enlargement by CT size criteria.  

OSSESOUS STRCUTURES:  No blastic or lytic lesions concerning for malignancy. 
Multilevel mild degenerative changes are noted.  

IMPRESSION:

1. Moderate fecal loading of the colon otherwise, no acute intraabdominal
process to explain patient's abdominal pain. 

2. Cirrhosis with post treatment changes from known RFA and TACE in the liver
and evidence of portal hypertension. Evaluation of residual disease cannot be
performed on this single phase examination.
